records.note: The English name has a documented occupational or nickname explanation from the small drum. Middle English and Old French dictionaries record several drum spellings. This is one origin of the English surname. Search spelling and family relationship independently.

records.title: Older Scots and English drum forms
records.note: Taborn(e), Tab(b)orn(e), Tabro(u)n(e), Tabrowne, Tabouryne, Tauburn(e), Taubroun, Tawbern(e), Tawbero(u)n, Tawbron, Talburn, Talborne, Talbrone, Talbroun, Talberone, Tabar(e), Taber, Tabuir, Talbert, Tabret, Tambour, Tabourn, Taburn, Taberett, Tawburn and Tabbern are dictionary forms or cited Middle English parallels. The dictionary dates tabour to c.1290 and taber to 1325 in the citations it lists.

records.title: Tábor · Tabor · Taborite
records.note: Tábor is a documented Czech place-based surname origin. The Czech town took its name from biblical Mount Tabor. The surname dictionary also lists a Bohemian Jewish habitational origin and South Slavic and Polish camp or fortification explanations.
links: Dictionary of American Family Names · Tabor

records.title: תָּבוֹר · Tavor · Thabor · Θαβώρ · Ἰταβύριον
records.note: Compare pointed Hebrew, transliteration, Greek biblical forms and the Greek historical Itabyrion. These are place-name records. The Hebrew lexicon treats the underlying etymology as uncertain. Atabyrion and Atabyrium remain comparison spellings to check against editions and geographic referents.
links: Hebrew and Aramaic Lexicon of the Old Testament · תבור

records.title: Ṭabarestān · Tabaristan · Ṭabarī · Tabīra · Tanbūr · Tambur
records.note: Ṭabarestān is a Caspian region. Tabīra is identified as a possible drum type in Iranica. Tanbūr refers to a family of stringed instruments. Each needs its own dated lexical record before a proposed connection to Tabor can be tested.
links: Encyclopædia Iranica · Ebn Esfandīār and the History of Ṭabarestān

records.title: ROBAT · REBAT · RIBAT · REVAT · ROVAT · RIVAT · RABAT
records.note: TABOR ⇄ ROBAT, TABER ⇄ REBAT, TABIR ⇄ RIBAT, TAVER ⇄ REVAT, TAVOR ⇄ ROVAT and TAVIR ⇄ RIVAT are literal character reversals. Rabat is a comparison form. Arabic ribāṭ has its own r-b-ṭ derivation. Search the reversed spellings without treating the reversal as a borrowing.

records.title: TABIR · TABRE · TAVER · TAVIR · TABORR and further variants
records.note: Intake and prior research leads also include Tabbor, Tabernor, Tabberner, Tabbernor, Tabiner, Tabner, Tabournier and Tabert. Validate a dated occurrence, language and person for each. The intake proposed TABOR in England by 1066. Prior research logged Tabour to 975 and a minstrel lead to 625. Exact manuscripts and folio references are still needed.

records.title: William Tabor · W6245, NC → SC → TN → AL
records.note: The pension transcription records his statement that he was born in Orange County, NC, served while living in Burke and Rutherford, then moved through Granville and Pendleton districts, SC, and several Tennessee counties before Shelby and Bibb counties, AL. Susannah's application says they married in Rutherford County in 1781. A Kernersville or Madison County descent requires intervening records.

records.title: Kernersville · Madison County · pre-Silk-Road ancestry
records.note: The existing family matrix is the starting point. Establish a documented parent–child chain generation by generation using deeds, probate, marriage, census, military and church records. The 1375 Taborite dating lead also needs a source that can be reconciled with Tábor's documented 1420 founding.
